FixpApplied.description: An optional application message telling the party that sends an idempotent flow which of its operations took effect, where no business message already says so.

from_seq_no.description: Where the run of operations that took effect starts.

message_count.description: How many operations in a row took effect.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

FixpApplied.title: FixpApplied

FixpContext.description: On a transport that several sessions share, names the session the following messages belong to and, when the flow is sequenced, where its numbering continues.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

next_seq_no.description: The number the sender's next application message will carry.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpContext.title: FixpContext

FixpEstablish.description: A client's request to tie a negotiated session to the very transport this message arrives on. After a disconnection it is sent again to re-bind.

credentials.description: Data that identifies the client, in a form the two parties agree on.

keepalive_interval.description: The longest the client stays silent, in milliseconds, before a heartbeat.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

next_seq_no.description: When the client's recoverable flow is bound again, the number its next application message will carry.

request_time.description: When the sender made this request. The answer repeats it, to show what it answers.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpEstablish.title: FixpEstablish

FixpEstablishmentAck.description: A server's acceptance of the binding. From here, application messages may flow.

keepalive_interval.description: The longest the server stays silent, in milliseconds, before a heartbeat.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

next_seq_no.description: If the server's flow is recoverable, the number its next application message will carry, so the client can ask for what it missed.

request_timestamp.description: The request_time of the Establish this message accepts.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpEstablishmentAck.title: FixpEstablishmentAck

FixpEstablishmentReject.description: A server's refusal of the binding.

establishment_reject_code.description: Why the server refused to bind the session.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

reason_text.description: Free text that says more about the code beside it.

request_timestamp.description: The request_time of the Establish this message refuses.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpEstablishmentReject.title: FixpEstablishmentReject

FixpEstablishmentRejectCode.description: Why a server would not bind the session to this transport.
FixpEstablishmentRejectCode.title: FixpEstablishmentRejectCode

FixpExchange.description: The messages of one session in the order they were sent, as a test case, a worked example or a captured log.

description.description: Free text about a record, for the people who read it.

exchange_steps.description: Each step of the exchange, in order.

id.description: The identifier of an exchange or a rules-of-engagement record.

multiplexed.description: Whether the transport carries other sessions too, so that Context takes the place of Sequence.

session_kind.description: Which of the two forms the session takes.

FixpExchange.title: FixpExchange

FixpExchangeStep.description: One step: a FIXP message, or a run of application messages whose content FIXP does not define, and the side that sent it.

application_message_count.description: How many application messages went out one after another. On a sequenced flow each takes the next sequence number.

sent_by.description: The side that sent this step.

FixpExchangeStep.title: FixpExchangeStep

FixpFinishedReceiving.description: Answers FinishedSending once the last message of the peer's flow has been processed. After it the session is finalized and its identifier is spent.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpFinishedReceiving.title: FixpFinishedReceiving

FixpFinishedSending.description: Says that the sender's flow has carried its last application message, which begins finalization. It is repeated as the heartbeat until the answer comes.

last_seq_no.description: The number carried by the flow's final application message.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpFinishedSending.title: FixpFinishedSending

FixpFlowType.description: How surely a flow is delivered. A flow is what one side of a session sends the other, leaving out session messages.
FixpFlowType.title: FixpFlowType

FixpMessage.description: One FIXP message, as its fields would be read from the wire before or after encoding.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

FixpMessage.title: FixpMessage

FixpMessageTemplate.description: Hands the peer a template or schema it needs to read messages in an encoding that templates drive. There is no fixed moment for sending it.

effective_time.description: When the template comes into force. Without it, the template applies at once.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

sofh_encoding_type.description: The code that the Simple Open Framing Header registers for the encoding a template is written for.

template_version.description: The template's version and format, for an encoding whose templates do not state them.

FixpMessageTemplate.title: FixpMessageTemplate

FixpMulticastFlowType.description: The delivery guarantee a multicast topic announces for its flow.
FixpMulticastFlowType.title: FixpMulticastFlowType

FixpNegotiate.description: A client's request to create a session under an identifier it has never used, stating the flow type it will send.

client_flow.description: The flow type of the application messages the client will send.

credentials.description: Data that identifies the client, in a form the two parties agree on.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

request_time.description: When the sender made this request. The answer repeats it, to show what it answers.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpNegotiate.title: FixpNegotiate

FixpNegotiationReject.description: A server's refusal to create a session. The server sends nothing more and closes the transport.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

negotiation_reject_code.description: Why the server refused to create the session.

reason_text.description: Free text that says more about the code beside it.

request_timestamp.description: The request_time of the Negotiate this message refuses.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpNegotiationReject.title: FixpNegotiationReject

FixpNegotiationRejectCode.description: Why a server refused to create a session.
FixpNegotiationRejectCode.title: FixpNegotiationRejectCode

FixpNegotiationResponse.description: A server's acceptance of a new session, stating the flow type it will send back.

credentials.description: Data that identifies the server to the client, for mutual authentication.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

request_timestamp.description: The request_time of the Negotiate this message accepts.

server_flow.description: The flow type of the application messages the server will send.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpNegotiationResponse.title: FixpNegotiationResponse

FixpNotApplied.description: An application message telling the party that sends an idempotent flow about a gap: a run of operations that did not take effect. That party's application decides what to do.

from_seq_no.description: Where the run of operations that failed to take effect starts.

message_count.description: How many operations in a row did not take effect.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

FixpNotApplied.title: FixpNotApplied

FixpParty.description: The side that sends a step.
FixpParty.title: FixpParty

FixpRetransmission.description: Introduces a batch of resent messages, which are numbered by counting from the number it gives. A request may be answered in several batches.

message_count.description: How many resent messages the batch holds.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

next_seq_no.description: The number the batch's first message carries.

request_timestamp.description: The request_time of the RetransmitRequest this batch answers.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpRetransmission.title: FixpRetransmission

FixpRetransmitReject.description: Refuses a RetransmitRequest, with a code saying why.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

reason_text.description: Free text that says more about the code beside it.

request_timestamp.description: The request_time of the RetransmitRequest this message refuses.

retransmit_reject_code.description: Why the sender will not resend the range.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpRetransmitReject.title: FixpRetransmitReject

FixpRetransmitRejectCode.description: Why a party will not resend the messages its peer asked for.
FixpRetransmitRejectCode.title: FixpRetransmitRejectCode

FixpRetransmitRequest.description: Asks the peer to resend some messages of its recoverable flow. A party has at most one such request open at a time.

from_seq_no.description: Where the requested run starts, by sequence number.

message_count.description: How many messages are asked for.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

request_time.description: When the request was made, which also tells this request apart from others.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

FixpRetransmitRequest.title: FixpRetransmitRequest

FixpRulesOfEngagement.description: What two counterparties agree on for one FIXP service, layer by layer, for the client and for the server.

description.description: Free text about a record, for the people who read it.

id.description: The identifier of an exchange or a rules-of-engagement record.

FixpRulesOfEngagement.title: FixpRulesOfEngagement

FixpSequence.description: Starts the numbering of a sequenced flow, so that the application messages after it are numbered by counting up from the value it carries. Sent when idle, it is also the heartbeat.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

next_seq_no.description: The number the sender's next application message will carry.

FixpSequence.title: FixpSequence

FixpSessionKind.description: The two forms of FIXP session.
FixpSessionKind.title: FixpSessionKind

FixpStackProfile.description: One side's choices at each layer of the stack: application, presentation, session, security and transport.

application_fix_version.description: The FIX version of the application messages, such as FIX.Latest.

application_recovery.description: Whether this side's applications recover lost messages themselves.

authentication_methods.description: How the parties prove who they are.

credentials_format.description: The form of the credentials this side sends, and how its peer checks them.

extension_packs.description: The FIX extension packs in use.

framing.description: What marks where one message ends and the next begins, such as the Simple Open Framing Header.

longest_keepalive_interval.description: The longest keep-alive interval, in milliseconds, that this side accepts from its peer.

message_encoding.description: How messages are encoded, such as Simple Binary Encoding.

message_schemas.description: The message schemas or templates the encoding uses.

network_protocols.description: Any other network protocols in use.

retransmission_limit.description: The most messages this side resends in answer to one RetransmitRequest.

service_pack.description: The FIX service pack, where the version has them.

shortest_keepalive_interval.description: The shortest keep-alive interval, in milliseconds, that this side accepts from its peer.

supported_flow_types.description: The flow types this side accepts or offers.

tls_version.description: The TLS version that protects the transport.

transports.description: The transports this side can use, for example TCP, or UDP with multicast.

FixpTerminate.description: Releases the session from its transport without ending the session, which can be bound again later. The peer answers with a Terminate, and after its own Terminate a party sends nothing more.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

reason_text.description: Free text that says more about the code beside it.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

termination_code.description: Why the party releases the session from the transport.

FixpTerminate.title: FixpTerminate

FixpTerminationCode.description: Why a party releases a session from its transport.
FixpTerminationCode.title: FixpTerminationCode

FixpTopic.description: A multicast publisher's notice that starts a flow and ties the session's short-lived identifier to a lasting subject. It is repeated so that late listeners can join.

flow.description: The flow type of a multicast topic's messages.

keepalive_interval.description: The publisher's heartbeat interval, in milliseconds.

message_kind.description: The class of this message, such as FixpNegotiate. It stands for FIXP's MessageType, which every message carries.

session_id.description: The session's identifier, which the client chooses and never uses again.

topic_classification.description: The lasting subject of a topic's messages, such as a product type or a market symbol.
